Create a sparse, atmospheric medieval mountain fortress beside a broad, shallow, muddy river or flooded plain. Surround it with rolling green-and-tan ground and steep, pale, heavily eroded mountains. Give the ground strongly rippled surfaces forming broad undulating slopes, exposed cream-colored ridges, shallow channels, and distant water edges. Use warm low sunlight, long shadows, and a partly cloudy sky.

At one end of the scene, position one large ruined stone castle on a rocky rise. Assemble its compact adjoining structures from a tall rectangular gatehouse or keep with a pointed-arched opening, several lower round and square towers, crenellated curtain walls, roofless interior chambers, broken wall sections, and scattered red banners and small red-tiled or conical roofs. Place pale boulders around its foundations.

From the castle, carry a long, straight fortified stone bridge or causeway across the water. Support it on a repeated sequence of broad masonry arches, line it with low battlements, and finish the far end with a small roofed gateway-like section. Beside the castle end, position a damaged wooden ramp, stairs, platforms, braces, and numerous irregular vertical piles rising from the water, some broken or leaning. Distribute a few isolated posts and debris across the flooded area.

Put patches of vivid low vegetation along the shoreline and one or two dense dark-green tree clusters near the bridge’s outer side. Leave the composition largely open and uncluttered, with the fortress and bridge as its only major built elements. Use generous empty space to emphasize their isolation, ruined condition, and dramatic scale.

deterministic_rule_draft.prompt:
Create a sparse, atmospheric medieval mountain fortress beside a broad, shallow, muddy river or flooded plain. Surround it with rolling green-and-tan ground and steep, pale, heavily eroded mountains. Give the ground strongly rippled surfaces forming broad undulating slopes, exposed cream-colored ridges, shallow channels, and distant water edges. Use warm low sunlight, long shadows, and a partly cloudy sky.

At one end of the scene, position one large ruined stone castle on a rocky rise. Assemble its compact adjoining structures from a tall rectangular gatehouse or keep with a pointed-arched opening, several lower round and square towers, crenellated curtain walls, roofless interior chambers, broken wall sections, and scattered red banners and small red-tiled or conical roofs. Place pale boulders around its foundations.

From the castle, carry a long, straight fortified stone bridge or causeway across the water. Support it on a repeated sequence of broad masonry arches, line it with low battlements, and finish the far end with a small roofed gateway-like section. Beside the castle end, position a damaged wooden ramp, stairs, platforms, braces, and numerous irregular vertical piles rising from the water, some broken or leaning. Distribute a few isolated posts and debris across the flooded area.

Put patches of vivid low vegetation along the shoreline and one or two dense dark-green tree clusters near the bridge’s outer side. Leave the composition largely open and uncluttered, with the fortress and bridge as its only major built elements. Use generous empty space to emphasize their isolation, ruined condition, and dramatic scale.
